plan.title: Fresh fish first
plan.summary: Salmon on day 1 and shrimp on day 2, while they are fresh. Tins, tofu and eggs keep the protein up for the rest of the week.

recipes.title: Cottage cheese bowl with blueberries and hemp seeds
steps: Stir the oats into the yogurt.
Spoon the cottage cheese alongside and top with the blueberries and hemp seeds.
Drizzle with honey.
recipes.why: A no-cook breakfast built on the cottage cheese.

recipes.title: Smoked salmon and egg toast
steps: Soft-boil the eggs for six and a half minutes, cool and peel.
Spread the cottage cheese over the toast and layer on the avocado and smoked salmon.
Halve the eggs on top and finish with lemon juice and pepper.
recipes.why: Uses the smoked salmon and an avocado half while they are good.

recipes.title: Tuna and white bean salad
steps: Boil the egg for eight minutes, cool, peel and quarter.
Toss the beans, cucumber, tomatoes and onion with the oil and lemon juice.
Pile onto the spinach and top with the tuna and egg.
recipes.why: A first-day lunch that starts on the spinach, cucumber and tomatoes.

recipes.title: Roasted salmon with asparagus and sweet potato
steps: Heat the oven to 220 C (425 F). Roast the sweet potato with half the oil and salt for fifteen minutes.
Add the asparagus and salmon to the tray, drizzle with the remaining oil and roast twelve minutes more.
Stir the garlic and lemon juice into the yogurt.
Serve with the yogurt sauce and lemon wedges.
recipes.why: Cooks both salmon fillets and the asparagus on day one, the two things that spoil fastest.

recipes.title: Shrimp and black bean tacos with lime crema
steps: Toss the shrimp with the chili powder and cumin and sear in the oil for two minutes a side.
Warm the beans in the same pan.
Stir half the lime juice into the yogurt and toss the cabbage with the rest.
Fill the tortillas with beans, shrimp, cabbage and avocado and top with crema, cilantro and jalapeno.
recipes.why: All the shrimp on day two, with the cilantro, a jalapeno and the ripest avocado.

recipes.title: Cod with tomatoes, olives and white beans
steps: Warm the garlic in the oil, add the tomatoes and cook until they burst, about five minutes.
Stir in the beans, olives and spinach.
Nestle the cod into the pan, cover and cook for eight minutes until it flakes.
Finish with parsley and a squeeze of lemon.
recipes.why: Finishes the cherry tomatoes and spinach; buy the cod on the day or keep it frozen.

recipes.title: Tofu and edamame fried rice with egg
steps: Cook the rice and spread it on a plate to cool for five minutes.
Brown the tofu in half the sesame oil and set aside. Scramble the eggs in the same pan and set aside.
Fry the carrot, garlic, ginger and edamame for three minutes, then add the rice.
Return the tofu and egg, add the soy sauce, remaining oil and green onions, and toss until hot.
recipes.why: A midweek dinner from the freezer and the cupboard, once the fresh fish is gone.

recipes.title: Tuna, pea and spinach pasta with lemon
steps: Boil the pasta, adding the peas for the last two minutes. Keep half a cup of the water.
Warm the garlic and capers in the oil, then add the spinach to wilt.
Toss in the pasta, peas, tuna, lemon and enough pasta water to loosen.
Serve with the parmesan.
recipes.why: Tins and frozen peas, so nothing fresh has to last until day five.

recipes.title: Shrimp and edamame coconut curry with rice
steps: Start the rice. Fry the garlic, ginger and curry powder in the oil for a minute.
Add the coconut milk, pepper, snap peas and edamame and simmer for six minutes.
Add the shrimp and cook for three minutes until pink.
Season with fish sauce and lime juice and serve over the rice.
recipes.why: Frozen shrimp for the weekend, thawed on the day.

recipes.title: Cottage cheese and spinach omelette with toast
steps: Wilt the spinach in the oil in a non-stick pan and spread it out.
Pour in the eggs and cook gently until nearly set.
Spoon the cottage cheese and parmesan over one half, fold and cook for a minute more.
Serve with the toast.
recipes.why: Ends the week on eggs and the last of the cottage cheese.

plan.title: Greens early, pantry late
plan.summary: Tofu, mushrooms and the soft greens are cooked in the first three days. Lentils, beans and tempeh carry the protein for the rest of the week.

recipes.title: Blueberry yogurt bowls with oats and walnuts
steps: Stir the oats and milk into the yogurt and leave for five minutes.
Divide between two bowls.
Top with the blueberries and walnuts and drizzle with honey.
recipes.why: Uses the blueberries, which will not last the week, and the open milk.

recipes.title: Feta and spinach scrambled eggs on pita
steps: Warm the oil in a non-stick pan and wilt the spinach with the tomatoes for a minute.
Add the eggs and stir gently until softly set.
Fold in the feta and serve on the toasted pita.
recipes.why: A savoury breakfast from the eggs, the spinach and some of the feta.

recipes.title: Hummus, cucumber and egg pitas
steps: Boil the eggs for eight minutes, cool, peel and quarter.
Toss the cucumber, tomatoes and spinach with the lemon juice.
Split the pitas, spread with hummus, and fill with the salad, egg and feta.
recipes.why: Day one's lunch: the opened hummus, the cucumber and the first of the tomatoes.

recipes.title: Crispy tofu with mushrooms, peppers and rice
steps: Start the rice. Toss the tofu with the cornstarch.
Fry the tofu in the vegetable oil over medium-high heat until golden on all sides, then set aside.
Stir-fry the mushrooms, peppers, garlic and ginger for five minutes, then add the edamame.
Return the tofu, add the soy sauce and sesame oil, and toss until glazed.
recipes.why: Cooks both blocks of tofu, the mushrooms and the peppers on the first night.

recipes.title: Kale and white bean pasta with parmesan
steps: Boil the pasta, adding the kale for the last three minutes. Keep a cup of the water.
Meanwhile, warm the garlic and red pepper flakes in the oil, then add the beans and tomatoes.
Toss in the drained pasta and kale with the lemon and enough pasta water to make a sauce.
Finish with the parmesan and basil.
recipes.why: Uses the kale and basil on day two and the last of the tomatoes.

recipes.title: Zucchini and chickpea shakshuka with feta
steps: Soften the onion and zucchini in the oil for six minutes, then add the garlic, cumin and paprika.
Stir in the tomatoes and chickpeas and simmer for ten minutes.
Make eight wells, crack in the eggs, cover and cook for six minutes until the whites are set.
Scatter with feta and serve with pita.
recipes.why: Both zucchini go in on day three, before they soften, with the rest of the feta.

recipes.title: Red lentil and spinach dal with rice
steps: Start the rice. Soften the onion in the oil, then add the garlic, ginger and curry powder for a minute.
Add the lentils, tomatoes, coconut milk and two cups of water and simmer for eighteen minutes.
Stir in the spinach until wilted and season to taste.
Serve over the rice with a spoonful of yogurt.
recipes.why: A pantry dinner for midweek, with a fresh bag of spinach stirred through.

recipes.title: Black bean and pepper quesadillas with yogurt-lime sauce
steps: Mix the beans, peppers, corn and cumin.
Spread over four tortillas, cover with cheddar and top with the remaining tortillas.
Cook in a dry pan for three minutes a side until crisp and melted.
Stir the lime juice into the yogurt and serve with the quesadillas and salsa.
recipes.why: The highest-protein dinner of the week, from tins and a block of cheddar.

recipes.title: Tempeh, broccoli and peanut noodles
steps: Soak the noodles in boiling water for eight minutes, adding the broccoli for the last three, then drain.
Brown the tempeh in the vegetable oil for six minutes.
Whisk the peanut butter, soy sauce, lime juice, garlic and sesame oil with four tablespoons of hot water.
Toss everything together with the carrot ribbons.
recipes.why: Tempeh keeps well, so it anchors the end of the week.

recipes.title: Egg fried rice with peas and edamame
steps: Cook the rice and spread it on a plate to cool for five minutes.
Scramble the eggs in half the vegetable oil and set aside.
Fry the carrot, peas and edamame in the rest of the oil for three minutes, then add the rice.
Return the eggs, add the soy sauce, sesame oil and green onions, and toss until hot.
recipes.why: A freezer-and-pantry dinner for the last night, when the fresh food is gone.

plan.title: Chicken first, then tacos
plan.summary: Raw chicken and turkey are cooked on days 1 and 2. Each dinner makes the next day's lunch, and two breakfasts take turns.

recipes.title: Yogurt and oat bowls with banana and almonds
steps: Stir the oats into the milk and yogurt and leave for five minutes, or overnight in the fridge.
Divide between two bowls.
Top with the banana, almonds and chia seeds, then drizzle with honey.
recipes.why: Uses the open milk and the big tub of yogurt for a breakfast that needs no cooking.

recipes.title: Spinach and cheddar scramble in tortillas
steps: Melt the butter in a non-stick pan over medium heat and wilt the spinach for a minute.
Pour in the eggs and stir slowly until just set, then fold in the cheddar.
Spoon into the warm tortillas and top with salsa.
recipes.why: Works through the eggs and spinach while both are fresh.

recipes.title: Egg, avocado and cheddar wraps
steps: Boil the eggs for eight minutes, cool under cold water, peel and slice.
Stir the lemon juice and hot sauce into the yogurt.
Spread the yogurt over the tortillas, layer on spinach, egg, avocado and cheddar, and roll up.
recipes.why: A first-day lunch from what is already open: one avocado, some spinach and the cheddar.

recipes.title: Lemon-garlic chicken with broccoli and rice
steps: Season the chicken with salt and pepper and brown it in the oil over high heat for five minutes.
Add the garlic, broccoli and carrots with a splash of water, cover and steam for five minutes.
Stir in the lemon juice and soy sauce and cook uncovered until the chicken is done.
Warm the rice and serve the chicken and vegetables over it.
recipes.why: Cooks all the raw chicken on day one, with the broccoli and the leftover rice.

recipes.title: Turkey and black bean tacos with peppers
steps: Soften the onion and peppers in the oil for five minutes.
Add the turkey, chili powder, cumin and salt and cook, breaking it up, until browned.
Stir in the beans and half the salsa and simmer for five minutes.
Fill the tortillas and top with cheddar, avocado and the rest of the salsa.
recipes.why: Uses the ground turkey on day two, before it turns, along with both peppers and the second avocado.

recipes.title: Roasted salmon with zucchini, tomatoes and quinoa
steps: Heat the oven to 220 C (425 F). Simmer the quinoa in two cups of water for fifteen minutes.
Toss the zucchini, tomatoes and garlic with the oil, oregano and salt on a large tray.
Roast for ten minutes, add the salmon skin side down, and roast twelve minutes more.
Serve over the quinoa with lemon.
recipes.why: Clears the zucchini and the cherry tomatoes; the salmon is the one fresh buy for midweek.

recipes.title: Beef and broccoli stir-fry with rice
steps: Start the rice. Toss the beef with the cornstarch and one tablespoon of the soy sauce.
Sear the beef in the vegetable oil over high heat for two minutes, then set it aside.
Stir-fry the broccoli, carrots, garlic and ginger with a splash of water for four minutes.
Return the beef, add the remaining soy sauce and the sesame oil, and toss for a minute.
recipes.why: Finishes the carrots and gives the week a fast dinner that reheats well.

recipes.title: Turkey meatballs in marinara with whole wheat pasta
steps: Mix the turkey, egg, breadcrumbs, garlic, oregano and half the parmesan and roll into sixteen balls.
Brown the meatballs in a wide pan for five minutes, turning once.
Pour in the marinara, cover and simmer for twelve minutes while the pasta boils.
Stir the spinach into the sauce to wilt, then serve over the pasta with the rest of the parmesan.
recipes.why: A second pack of turkey later in the week, with spinach stirred in to use up the bag.

recipes.title: Skillet chicken thighs with carrots and couscous
steps: Rub the chicken with cumin and paprika and brown it in the oil for four minutes a side.
Add the onion, carrots and garlic and cook for three minutes.
Pour in the broth, cover and simmer for ten minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Stir in the couscous, cover, take off the heat for five minutes, then finish with lemon and parsley.
recipes.why: One pan, and it makes Sunday's lunch as well.

recipes.title: Seared sirloin with sweet potato and green beans
steps: Roast the sweet potato with the oil and half the salt at 220 C (425 F) for twenty-five minutes.
Boil the green beans for four minutes and drain.
Season the steak and sear it in a hot pan for three minutes a side, adding the butter and garlic at the end.
Rest the steak for five minutes, slice, and serve with the vegetables and the pan butter.
recipes.why: A simple end to the week that needs nothing left over.
